author: 0xydendrum
hardware: NVIDIA RTX 3060 12 GB, Intel i5-14600KF, 32 GB DDR4-3200, Windows 11; quality reference NVIDIA RTX A6000 48 GB
software: llama.cpp b11798 (commit ec0da70e9); spilltune 0.2.0; PyTorch/transformers 5.5.0 for F5 and F7
speed_test: spilltune's 4 prompts (math, code, explain, writing) x 192 tokens, temperature 0, 1 chat at a time, context 4096; overall = total tokens / total time
quality_test: 300 MMLU-Pro + 150 GSM8K test questions, fixed seed, temperature 0; paired difference vs same GGUF fully in VRAM; no loss = diff + margin >= 0

findings.claim: A confidence cut-off (--spec-draft-p-min 0.7) roughly doubles prose speed for a DFlash helper on a spilled Gemma 4 31B, with no quality loss.
findings.baseline_desc: same helper (DFlash, 16 guesses) without the cut-off; no helper = 3.4
findings.n: 4 prompts x 192 tokens per setup; 450 questions for quality

findings.claim: An MTP helper (3 guesses, cut-off 0.7) makes Gemma 4 26B-A4B with experts in RAM 1.50x faster on every prompt kind, with no quality loss; DFlash reaches 1.14x.
findings.baseline_desc: llama-server defaults, same model and placement
findings.n: 4 prompts x 192 tokens per trial, 12 trials per run, 2 runs; 450 questions for quality

findings.claim: On a spilled Gemma 4 31B, MTP is fastest at 6 guesses (8 to 12 are slower on every prompt kind); with the cut-off it reaches 2.61x the defaults.
Serving many requests at once gives spilled models far more total throughput than any single-chat setting, with no quality loss at 16 slots and an 8-bit cache.
findings.n: 1 prompt per request, levels 1/4/8/16/32; 450 questions for quality

findings.claim: Negative result: an n-gram snapshot memory does not repair Qwen3.5-2B carved into experts (34% active); after distillation perplexity is 16.05 with it vs 16.01 without.
findings.baseline_desc: same distillation with no memory; dense model 11.85; carved untrained 30.58

findings.claim: CPU threads, --fit-target margins and tensor-level offload were flat; driver VRAM spill halved speed; 32K context cost 7 to 11%; n-gram and small-model helpers gave nothing.

Negative result: a forward-filled (training-free) Engram-style n-gram table predicts at most 2.73% of the hidden-state gap a healed dense-to-MoE carve of Qwen3.5-2B leaves, even with canonical keys, layer 0 and a learned context gate + value projection, and closes 0.43% of the perplexity gap (bars 5% and 5 pp).
findings.metric: held-out WikiText-2 R² of the carve's hidden-state gap (rank-128 code, full-width error)
findings.baseline_desc: no memory (R² 0); preregistered bar 0.05; A0 (raw keys, probes 3-23) 0.0085
findings.n: 65,536 held-out tokens per eval set; 95% CI by block bootstrap over 64 sequences; single seed
